caveats: Verdict assumes a database where concurrent UPDATEs of the same row serialize via row locks (e.g. Postgres read-committed, the production engine per hc/settings.py:125-141); deployment model is UNCONFIRMED.
Assumes each ping request runs on its own DB connection and transaction, as separately served web requests do.
subclaims.reason: In R1 each ping request loads its own Check at hc/api/views.py:50 and calls Check.ping at hc/api/views.py:82, so the two sides are separate transactions on separate connections. Inside ping the counter UPDATE (hc/api/models.py:422-425), the re-read (hc/api/models.py:426) and the Ping INSERT (hc/api/models.py:429-445) all run inside one transaction.atomic block (hc/api/models.py:388). Under read-committed the first UPDATE holds the row lock, so the second same-row UPDATE blocks until the first transaction commits, and the two refresh SELECTs therefore return consecutive n_pings values rather than the same one. There is no autocommit gap between save and refresh for a concurrent commit to slip into. So two concurrent pings cannot share one Ping.n through this path in this tree.

caveats: Needs two concurrent ping requests to the same check whose load-to-save windows overlap, one carrying action=start.
Needs a DB where the stale-read-then-UPDATE interleaving is possible (e.g. Postgres read-committed, the production engine per hc/settings.py:120-138); deployment model is UNCONFIRMED.
Relies on Django Model.save() writing all columns (no update_fields) and per-request DB connections, both outside this tree.
subclaims.reason: In R3 each ping request loads its own Check copy at hc/api/views.py:37 and calls Check.ping at hc/api/views.py:58, e.g. POST .../start (hc/api/urls.py:33) racing POST .../log or a plain success ping (hc/api/urls.py:34,31) for the same check. The start side sets last_start at hc/api/models.py:310 and commits it with Check.save at hc/api/models.py:337, while the other side loaded last_start=None before that commit and still holds None at its own save (hc/api/models.py:337) because log/ign never touch last_start (hc/api/models.py:312-315) or the stale-None success path keeps it None (hc/api/models.py:318-322). R3 ping (hc/api/models.py:303) has no transaction.atomic and no select_for_update, so each save is a separate autocommit UPDATE and Django writes all columns including the stale last_start, letting the second UPDATE overwrite the committed start under read-committed. The switch window spans whole DB round-trips that release the GIL, and separate workers share no GIL at all, so CPython with the GIL can interleave here.
